identity.title: DEBATE: Could God Be Evil? | Alex O'Connor vs Max Baker-Hytch

content.coverageNote: The complete sole English ASR track was read from opening music through farewell and outro. It includes substantive discussion from 03:37 to 1:28:03, with no material uncaptioned speech gap. The recorded technical interruption at 50:18–50:42 is followed by Max restating his argument. The final caption ends approximately two seconds beyond the nominal duration, an ASR tail rather than missing debate. Raw disfluencies and spelling errors remain unchanged. Evaluate attribution move by move; verify any below-high attribution or material lexical uncertainty using bounded audio.

participants.basis: Full-source review identifies only two substantive advocates. Cameron introduces the participants, neutrally summarizes the challenge and transitions, monitors time, and handles a technical interruption. His abstract reading summarizes the topic and adds no independent argumentative burden. No substantive host advocacy or primary-speaker scope exception is present.

format.motionInterpretation: O’Connor uses evil-god symmetry to challenge confidence in a wholly good God, not to advocate actual evil-god existence. Baker-Hytch accepts the limited symmetry of reversing major theodicies but disputes the ambitious equal-plausibility claim through natural-theological, intrinsic-coherence, and comparative-world arguments. Evaluate their announced qualifications, concessions, and the late loving-versus-malicious reframing; do not impose a burden to prove atheism or Christianity as a whole.

duplicateAudit.distinctExistingSpeakerDebates: The existing O’Connor–Baker-Hytch argument-from-reason conversation concerns a different topic and video. Their team problem-of-evil exchange and Baker-Hytch’s Baggini discussion are also distinct recordings.
